title: Sindhu and Lakshya Sen Complete an Indian Double at the Hylo Open
excerpt: Sindhu beat Kjaersfeldt 21-12, 21-14 and Sen beat defending champion Christie 21-17, 21-10 as India took both singles titles at the Super 500 event in Saarbrücken.
body:
• P. V. Sindhu beat Denmark's Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt 21-12, 21-14 to win the women's singles title at the Hylo Open in Saarbrücken, Germany, on Sunday, November 1.
  • Lakshya Sen defeated defending champion Jonatan Christie of Indonesia 21-17, 21-10 to take the men's singles crown at the same Super 500 event.
  • Sindhu is the first Indian woman to win the Hylo Open since the tournament began in 1988, and she did not drop a game all week.
  • It is the first time in four years that two Indians have won singles titles at the same BWF World Tour event of Super 500 level or above.

India finished the Hylo Open with both singles titles on Sunday, as P. V. Sindhu and Lakshya Sen won their finals in straight games at the Saarlandhalle in Saarbrücken. Sindhu beat eighth seed Line Hojmark Kjaersfeldt of Denmark 21-12, 21-14, and Sen beat fourth seed and defending champion Jonatan Christie of Indonesia 21-17, 21-10. Both finals lasted 39 minutes.

Sindhu's flawless week

Sindhu, the second seed, controlled her final from the start. She led 11-8 at the interval in the first game, then reeled off seven straight points from 14-12 to close it 21-12 in 17 minutes. In the second game she moved ahead 11-7, stretched the lead to 19-11, and sealed the title on a net error by Kjaersfeldt, according to ANI's report of the final. The win extended Sindhu's head-to-head record against the Dane to seven wins in eight meetings.

https://www.instagram.com/reel/DfAX7fqRRLr/

The title capped a week in which the 31-year-old, a two-time Olympic medallist and former world champion, did not lose a single game. She beat the UAE's Prakriti Bharath 21-10, 21-10 in the first round, France's Rosy Oktavia Pancasari 21-9, 21-6 in the second, Germany's Amalie Schulz 21-12, 21-10 in the quarter-finals, and compatriot Anmol Kharb 21-13, 21-16 in the semi-finals — the first international meeting between the two Indians. It is Sindhu's second BWF World Tour title of 2026, after the Japan Open in July, and it came one week after she finished runner-up at the French Open, where she lost the final to world No. 1 An Se Young of South Korea.

"It has been an amazing two weeks, I would say. Hats off to my whole team; we've been planning accordingly."

— P. V. Sindhu

Sen ends his wait

For Sen, the seventh seed, the title was his second at this tournament, seven years after he won it in 2019 when it was called the SaarLorLux Open. Ranked world No. 14 coming into the week, he beat a player ranked eight places above him: Christie, the world No. 6, was defending the title he won last year. Sen built a 16-9 lead in the second game, earned 10 match points after a successful line-call review, and converted the next point, ANI reported. In the semi-finals he had beaten France's Toma Junior Popov 21-17, 21-13.

The Hylo Open is Sen's seventh BWF World Tour title and his first of 2026, ending a drought that stretched back to the Australian Open in November 2025. He had reached the All England final earlier this season without converting it.

"It's been quite some time since I've won a tournament, so it feels really good to play this well. The last two matches that I played were really top-quality opponents, and I managed to beat them convincingly."

— Lakshya Sen

What it means

India was the only country to win two titles at the Hylo Open, a BWF World Tour Super 500 event with $500,000 in prize money, now in its 39th edition. Two Indians winning singles titles at the same World Tour event at Super 500 level or above had not happened in four years — the last instance cited by BadmintonPlanet was the 2022 India Open. For Sindhu, back-to-back finals in Paris and Saarbrücken mark her strongest run of the season; for Sen, a title after a year of near-misses restores momentum heading into the final stretch of the tour season.
